transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Oliver Reyes (Redwood CSM), Alicia Ramos (Bellwether Head of Platform), Derek Moon (Lead Backend), Priya Singh (Security & Compliance), Tom Gallagher (Product)
summary: Kickoff for Bellwether Commerce onboarding. Discussed integration approach for Redwood API, data residency and security requirements for private deployments, initial performance targets, and pilot success criteria. Agreed next steps: send onboarding runbook and pricing, run benchmarks, schedule security deep-dive.
topics: security and compliance (KMS, audit logs, SSO)
body:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Alicia Ramos (Bellwether): Hi, Alicia here, head of platform. excited to get this moving.
[00:18] Derek Moon (Bellwether): Derek, I run the backend services for personalization and catalog.
[00:22] Tom Gallagher (Bellwether): Tom, PM on the search and recommendations roadmap.
[00:27] Priya Singh (Bellwether): Priya, security and compliance. I'll own the compliance checklist.
[00:33] Maya Chen (Redwood): Great. Samir and Oliver are on from Redwood — Samir will cover the technical plan, Oliver will be your CSM.
[00:40] Samir Patel (Redwood): Hey all. quick note on agenda — integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), benchmark targets, pilot success metrics, and an ops runbook.
[00:52] Tom Gallagher (Bellwether): Our immediate goal is to replace an in-house ranker for product suggestions with something faster and cheaper. latency under 80ms p90 ideally, and cost per query needs to be under $0.002 average.
[01:05] Derek: Just to add, we have bursty traffic during flash sales; sustained qps is around 3500 but peak bursts to ~12k for 10-15 minutes.
[01:18] Maya: Good — helps us size. Priya, from compliance perspective, anything blocking for hosted?
[01:25] Priya: We prefer VPC/private for now. PCI/NDA concerns plus we need audit logs and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Also SSO/SAML, role-based access. We need SOC2 and ISO27001 paperwork.
[01:40] Oliver Reyes (Redwood): We can support private deployments with a customer-managed control plane; we have KMS integrations and audit log exports. We'll send the security pack.
[01:50] Priya: Awesome. can you also provide details on data retention and how long kv cache artifacts are persisted? we don't want any persistent PII.
[02:02] Samir: Sure. Redwood keeps ephemeral KV cache in memory by default; any persistent caching is opt-in and can be routed to customer-managed storage in the VPC. I'll include configuration snippets. note — sometimes the transcript says K-V cash in the docs, so we'll send clarified wording.
[02:20] Alicia: Thanks. on the integration side, our stack is Node + k8s. we want to use the SDK and have a sidecar option for lower latency — is that supported?
[02:33] Samir: Yes. SDKs for Node are available. for k8s we offer a sidecar pattern for private deployments and a containerized runtime for Dedicated. sidecar helps reduce RTT for short-lived requests. will share example helm charts.
[02:50] Derek: Any special kernel or quantization requirements for the model? our infra team is concerned about mixed-precision and the cost differences.
[02:58] Samir: We recommend int8/4 quantization for cost-sensitive workloads. Redwood's runtime will pick kernels based on the model and sequence length. for the initial pilot we'll suggest a 4-bit quantized variant and measure quality against your eval set.
[03:18] Tom: For the pilot, we can provide a 48-hour sample of production traffic anonymized. what metrics do you need?
[03:25] Samir: Token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and throughput at different batch sizes. also end-to-end latency from SDK to response.
[03:35] Maya: Let's capture success criteria: 1) p95 latency <= 120ms for the API call in the hosted/dedicated context, 2) cost per query within target, 3) no data residency or PII leakage. agreed?
[03:48] Alicia: Agreed, with note that for private we'll expect p95 under 80ms.
[03:54] Priya: We'll need a security deep-dive — key rotation, encrypted logs, and retention policies. also legal will want a DPA and data flow diagram.
[04:05] Oliver: We'll attach our standard DPA and a draft network diagram. we'll also include the SOC2 and ISO attestations.
[04:12] Derek: On the deployment model: do you recommend starting hosted for speed or go straight to private so we don't migrate later?
[04:20] Samir: Good question. Recommend a two-phase approach: start hosted for the pilot to iterate on prompts and model choices quickly, then move to private once traffic and security needs are validated. we can pin model versions to avoid regressions.
[04:35] Alicia: Concern: migrating later could be painful for traffic patterns. can you guarantee no API changes?
[04:40] Samir: The API surface is consistent across modes; differences are in routing and infra. there may be config differences for caching and network egress, but we'll provide a migration checklist.
[04:53] Tom: Will we be able to do canary rollouts for model updates?
[04:57] Oliver: Yes, Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback policies. we'll demonstrate that in the ops runbook.
[05:05] Priya: A few more security Qs — do you support customer-managed HSM for keys? how are audit logs exported?
[05:12] Samir: Yes, HSM/KMS options. we stream audit logs to S3 or your logging endpoint inside the VPC. logs can be configured to exclude request bodies that contain PII.
[05:24] Priya: Ok, will need sample log schemas and retention controls.
[05:29] Maya: We'll attach those. also we'll share the onboarding runbook which includes example Helm charts, SDK snippets, and troubleshooting tips.
[05:40] Derek: For the benchmarking — do you need us to run any client-side harness or will Redwood run the tests from their environment?
[05:48] Samir: We can do both. Redwood can run controlled benchmarks against a sandbox model in our infra, and we can send a small client harness for you to run inside your network to measure e2e latency.
[05:59] Tom: timeline — we're hoping to have pilot in two weeks?
[06:03] Maya: Two weeks is ambitious but possible. propose: week 1 - onboarding and shared runbook; week 2 - benchmarking and initial sample run; week 3 - review and decision on private vs dedicated.
[06:18] Alicia: That works for us if we can get the security pack quickly.
[06:23] Oliver: We'll aim to send the security pack and runbook by Friday (2026-10-09).
[06:29] Priya: Also want to invite legal for a short procurement sync; can that happen the week after the pilot?
[06:35] Maya: Yes, we'll coordinate.
[06:40] Maya: Any other questions?
[06:42] Derek: One small thing — how do you handle model rollback if quality regresses?
[06:47] Samir: We have pinned model versions and automatic fallback to a previous variant. plus we can set quality monitors tied to your eval prompt set. if a regression is detected it triggers an alert and rollback policy.
[06:58] Tom: Great. can you also include sample eval scripts?
[07:02] Samir: Yep, we'll include eval harness and a sample prompt set.
[07:08] Maya: Ok let's recap actions: Samir does benchmarking plan and runs tests; Maya sends pricing and runbook; Alicia provides traffic sample; Priya schedules security deep-dive.
[07:22] Alicia: I'll send the anonymized traffic slice by Monday.
[07:26] Priya: I'll send a list of compliance questions and invite legal to the follow-up.
[07:33] Oliver: I'll set up the follow-up meetings and share calendar invites.
[07:38] Maya: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc links and next steps.
[07:45] Meeting end.

Notes and links mentioned in call:
- Onboarding runbook (to be shared): includes helm charts, SDK examples, sidecar patterns
- Security pack: SOC2, ISO certifications, DPA template, log schema samples
- Benchmark spreadsheet: token-level latency, cost per 1k tokens, throughput by batch size
- Eval harness and sample prompt set

Transcription artifacts: occasional mis-hearings: 'K-V cash' for KV cache; 'side car' split as two words; some speaker overlaps labeled as 'Speaker 2' in the raw recording.

End of transcript.
